subject: Security and KMS follow-up: next steps and evidence

Subject: Security and KMS follow-up: next steps and evidence

Hi Alex / Nina,

Great meeting this morning - thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can keep momentum on the procurement path:

1) SOC 2 status
- Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in-scope for our hosted service. I've attached a summary of our report (redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf). We can provide a redacted report under NDA; our Security team can also respond to any SOC-related follow-ups you have.

2) Encryption & key management (KMS/HSM)
- In-transit: All traffic is TLS 1.2+ by default.
- At-rest: We use envelope encryption. For hosted/dedicated customers we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and Azure Key Vault.
- BYOK/HSM: For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) we support integration with customer HSMs; for hosted we support BYOK via external KMS where customers control keys.
- Key rotation: supported; we recommend rotating DEKs per your policy. We never persist plaintext keys in our backend.

3) Audit and logs
- Key usage logs and access audit trails are available via the Redwood Console and can be exported to your SIEM (CloudWatch/Cloud Logging/Blob storage).

4) Vendor questionnaire + evidence
- Attached: redwood-kms-whitepaper.pdf for architecture and a short SOC2 summary. If you want, we can start the vendor security questionnaire now - will need a contact for any additional clarifying questions.

Next steps I propose:
- You share the vendor questionnaire (if you haven't already) - I see you may have started one.
- I'll loop in our infra/security engineer for a technical deep-dive to cover HSM/BYOK specifics.
- Provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report under NDA if required.

Would Thursday or Friday next week work for a ~45m technical call? Also please confirm who should be the point person for procurement/security artifacts.

Thanks,

Thanks Camila - that recap is helpful. A few follow-ups from our side:

- BYOK vs. managed KMS: Can you confirm whether customers on the hosted plan can operationally bring their own key material (BYOK) using AWS KMS/Cloud KMS for envelope encryption, or is BYOK limited to Dedicated/Private deployments?
- HSM: If we need hardware-backed KMS/HSM guarantees, is that only available for Private deployments? Any reference architectures for an HSM-backed key store?
- Key rotation & re-encryption: If we rotate a CMK, how does that affect existing encrypted data / cached models? Do you require re-encryption of stored data or is envelope key rotation seamless?
- Audit logs: we need key usage logs with mTLS authentication events and the ability to push logs to our Splunk instance. Is this available out-of-the-box or does it need engineering work?

I've attached the vendor questionnaire we started (finbank-vendor-questionnaire.xlsx). Nina (cc) will own the security questionnaire completion. We'd also like to review a redacted SOC 2 Type II report if available.

Subject: Re: Security and KMS follow-up: next steps and evidence

Alex - great questions, and thanks for attaching the questionnaire. Answers below at a high level; Aditya (cc) from our infra team can join the tech call to go deeper into the HSM/BYOK mechanics.

1) BYOK on hosted vs Dedicated/Private
- Hosted: We support BYOK via customer-managed CMKs using supported cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault). This is implemented via envelope encryption where the customer CMK wraps a data encryption key (DEK) that encrypts the application data.
- Dedicated/Private: For Private deployments we can additionally integrate with on-prem HSM appliances (PKCS#11 compatible) for hardware-backed key storage.

2) HSM and reference architecture
- HSM-backed keys are available for Private deployments. For hosted customers that require FIPS/PII HSM guarantees, we recommend Dedicated w/ customer-managed KMS or a Private deployment. I'll attach a simple diagram (kms-diagram.png) and our whitepaper covers typical patterns.

3) Key rotation & re-encryption
- Envelope key rotation is designed to be seamless: when a CMK rotates, new DEKs are encrypted with the new CMK; existing ciphertexts remain decryptable as long as the wrapping CMK is retained for historical DEKs. If you require re-encryption, we can run a rewrap job, but it is not required for continuity.
- For cached model state (KV caches), we maintain encryption at rest and rotate DEKs transparently; there is no service interruption.

4) Audit logs & SIEM integration
- We surface key usage and access logs in the Redwood Console and provide log export endpoints to push to CloudWatch / Cloud Logging / Azure Monitor. For Splunk, we can forward logs via an HTTP collector or S3 ingestion. mTLS events and API key usage are included in the audit trail. Aditya can outline the exact fields we emit on the call.

Next steps:
- We'll ingest the vendor questionnaire you sent and start populating answers.
- Proposed tech deep-dive: Thursday 2026-09-03 14:00 PT (45m) - Aditya + Camila + Marissa. Please confirm or propose an alternate time.
- We'll prepare a redacted SOC2 Type II report and share under NDA (soc2-report-redacted.pdf).
